LearningGoals: Comprehend how the sign of the leading coefficient of a polynomial function affects the end behavior.
Create equations for polynomial functions with specific end behavior.
SourceAuthority: Local Kendall Hunt archival teacher/student pages; AccessIM v360 excluded

CoreMathWorkedExample.Question: Describe the left and right ends of f(x)=-2x^3+7x.
Steps: Leading term -2x^3 dominates. For x large positive it is negative
for x large negative it is positive.

ActivitySections: 9.2: The Case of Unexpected End Behavior
GradingRubric: teacher verifies diagrams, graphs, card work and explanation

FirstPartyCoolDown.Prompt: Give an odd-degree polynomial that goes up on the left and down on the right.
FirstPartyCoolDown.Expected: -x^3 or any odd degree with negative leading coefficient.
